title: Prune a dead rose cane just above its bud with bypass secateurs, holding the cutting as it parts
instruction: Cut out the dead stem on the rose bush and put it in the bin.
context: Removing dead wood is routine rose and shrub care: cut the dead cane back into green wood just above a bud with bypass secateurs, without cutting a live cane, removing the bud or dropping the cutting into the plant. The physical difficulty is squeezing the secateurs hard enough to part a 4.5 mm cane (3.5 N m at the jaws) among close neighbours while the other hand already holds the cane beyond the cut. Real trials use non-perishable, load-calibrated stand-in canes, so nothing wilts or varies.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the left), heights are above the table top, and directions are degrees counterclockwise from +x, seen from above. A free 3 kg terracotta pot, 22 cm across the rim and 7.5 cm tall, holding 1.2 kg of gravel, then dry floral foam, then 1.5 cm of dry potting soil (9 mm below the rim), stands with its centre at (0.363, 0.010). Six stand-in rose canes of dry round rattan core (basketry centre cane) stand in it, each pushed 6 cm into the foam along its lean; the printable 1:1 rig_template.svg gives every base, lean and direction. Five are live canes, 7 mm rattan core painted matte green, with silk rose leaves taped on above 11 to 14 cm: A, base (0.303, -0.007), leaning 50 degrees from upright toward 140 degrees, 26 cm above the soil, square-cut tip, no flower; B, base (0.351, -0.008), 50 degrees toward 102 degrees, 29 cm, silk rose in tight bud; C, base (0.380, 0.057), 40 degrees toward 72 degrees, 30 cm, open red silk rose; D, base (0.416, 0.029), 35 degrees toward 27 degrees, 30 cm, silk rose in tight bud; E, base (0.416, -0.027), 40 degrees toward -8 degrees, 27 cm, square-cut tip, no flower. The dead cane leaves the soil at (0.345, -0.037) and leans 55 degrees from upright toward 122 degrees, between A and B, which are 5.3 cm and 5.0 cm from it at its bud. It is 4.5 mm rattan core, 31 cm long above the soil and leafless, with a red 4 mm flat-back half-round bead (2 mm tall) glued on as its bud 12.5 cm along it, facing 212 degrees; it is painted matte green up to 2 cm beyond the bud's top and matte brown from there to its square-cut tip. Bypass secateurs (ARS 120DX, named for identification only), 195 mm long with a 49 mm cutting edge, 160 g, with red plastic-covered handles, a steel blade and a black steel hook, lie flat and open on the table with the pivot at (0.220, -0.130) and the jaws pointing toward 27 degrees; their spring holds them open. A free open black plastic garden tub, 26 cm across the top and 12 cm tall, stands at (0.260, 0.370). Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Measured after the trial with a tape measure on the plant, and from the video. Positions on the dead cane are measured along its axis. The original bud is the small red bud on the dead cane at the start. The stub is the part of the dead cane still in the pot at the end; the cutting is the piece the first cut frees. A good cut leaves the stub's cut face 3 to 15 mm beyond the top of the original bud, so a good first cut frees a cutting 16.6 to 17.8 cm long; the brown wood starts 20 mm beyond the bud's top. The bud is intact if no blade has touched it and it is still on the stub within 3 mm of its starting place, with the stub reaching past its top. Held means both fingers of one gripper are closed on the cutting (in the simulation: the gripper closed to at most the cutting's width plus 6 mm, with both finger-pad middles within 4 mm of its surface). The cutting falls if no gripper holds it at the moment the blades part it from the stem, or if at any later moment no gripper holds it and some part of it drops 3 cm or more while its middle is not over the bin's opening (seen from above). Lowering it into the bin and letting go over the opening is not a fall; bouncing out of the bin onto the table is. In the bin means not held, both ends of the cutting over the bin's opening seen from above (the bin upright within 30 degrees), and its lowest point below the rim. 0 at any moment, and it stays 0: a blade presses into a live cane (one of the five) hard enough to mark it (in the simulation, with 10 N or more); any cut passes through or below the original bud, a blade touches the bud, or the bud is no longer attached at its starting place; the cutting falls; the pot moves more than 2 cm or tilts more than 10 degrees; a cane breaks other than at the blades (real trials only; canes cannot break in the simulation); the secateurs fall off the table (secateurs left in the bin are not a fall; they only miss 1.0). Otherwise, by the state at the end: 0 the dead cane was not cut; doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0. 0.25 the dead cane was cut and the original bud is intact, but the first cut or the stub's final end is outside 3 to 15 mm beyond the bud; trimming the stub later does not raise this. 0.5 the first cut and the stub's final end are both 3 to 15 mm beyond the bud and the bud is intact, but the cutting is not in the bin (still held, or laid down elsewhere without falling). 0.75 as for 0.5 and the cutting is in the bin, but the 1.0 conditions have not all held for the last 1 s. 1.0 as for 0.75, and also: the secateurs lie on the table, flat within 20 degrees, with no part over the pot or in or over the tub; every fingertip is at least 5 cm from the secateurs, every cane and the cutting; neither end of the cutting moves 5 mm or more between any two samples over the last 1 s; and all of these hold together for that whole 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: One prepared dead-cane stand-in is used up per trial; the live canes, pot, template, secateurs and tub are reused. Prepare dead canes in a batch beforehand (they keep indefinitely): 37 cm lengths of dry 4.5 mm round rattan core, never soaked, stored indoors; bud bead glued 18.5 cm from the bottom; matte green below 2.4 cm above the bud's middle, matte brown above. Before the first trial of a session, check three spares from the batch with the luggage-scale test in the README. Insert each new dead cane into the same template hole, 6 cm deep at 55 degrees, bud facing 212.2 degrees. Replace a live cane if a blade has marked its paint. Reopen the secateurs on their marks; empty the tub.
fidelity: Canes are rigid round rods; leaves and flowers are visual only. The dead cane is 4.5 mm, like a rose's upper stem (published mean 4.64 mm), and parts only after the blade presses it with 142.25 N, a published rose shear strength times its section (3.5 N m at the jaw), at two samples 50 ms apart, against 40 N per finger. The rattan stand-in is checked to need that torque within 25%. Held is judged from finger positions; tiny later trimmings are not modelled.
